items.stem: You add an output parser to a LangChain chain. What should you still do?

options.text: Validate the parsed result and handle the case where the model returns invalid structure
options.rationale: Correct: parsers can fail, so validation and a fallback are still required.

options.text: Assume the model always returns valid structured output
options.rationale: Models can and do return malformed output.

options.text: Remove all error handling once a parser is present
options.rationale: Parsers do not remove the need for error handling.

options.text: Skip tests because the parser guarantees correctness
options.rationale: A parser guarantees neither validity nor correctness.

items.explanation: Correct: parsers can fail, so validation and a fallback are still required.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO practices make a tool-using LangChain app safer? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Validate tool arguments the model produces before executing them
options.rationale: Correct: model-produced arguments are untrusted and must be validated.

options.text: Constrain what each tool is allowed to do
options.rationale: Correct: least-privilege tools limit the blast radius of mistakes.

options.text: Let the model call any tool with any arguments
options.rationale: Unconstrained tool calls are a safety risk.

options.text: Hide tool errors from logs and tracing
options.rationale: Hiding errors prevents diagnosis and monitoring.

items.explanation: Correct: model-produced arguments are untrusted and must be validated.

items.stem: A LangChain chain fails intermittently in production and is hard to diagnose. What is the first thing to add?

options.text: Tracing/observability so each step's input and output can be inspected
options.rationale: Correct: step-level tracing is what makes intermittent failures diagnosable.
Prompt length does not help diagnose failures.

options.text: A larger model with no logging
options.rationale: Without logging the failure is still opaque.
Removing components blindly is not a diagnostic step.

items.explanation: Correct: step-level tracing is what makes intermittent failures diagnosable.
